articles.title: Nearly one in five AI researchers already expected an extinction scenario from AI back in 2024
articles.snippet: Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon sparked an intense debate about existential AI risks with a single tweet. OpenAI researcher Daniel Selsam warns of a "ticking time bomb," and a former Deepmind researcher says AI could kill us all. articles.snippet: arXiv:2609.13437v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Scientific research is a continuous process that emphasizes inheritance. Methods developed by predecessors are often expanded upon by new researchers to explore more novel and in-depth scientific questions. However, the change of lab staff, such as student graduation, leads to a lack of personnel capable of replicating methods. Methods that have been developed with significant effort and resources cannot be continued. articles.summary: LabAgent is a proposed reproduce-and-discovery harness that helps research labs preserve and continue methods across staff turnover by using AI agents for scientific discovery.

articles.title: TimeThink: Eliciting Compositional Reasoning in Timeseries Large Language Models
articles.snippet: arXiv:2609.13457v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Timeseries multimodal large language models (TS-MLLMs) have recently begun leveraging the reasoning capabilities of large language models (LLMs) for question-answering tasks. articles.summary: TimeThink is proposed to elicit compositional reasoning in timeseries multimodal LLMs, addressing their failure to capture dynamic temporal patterns and provide explicit explanations for high-stakes uses like healthcare.

articles.title: Root-Cause Attribution Is a Search Problem: Continual Search for Long-Horizon Agent Failures
articles.snippet: arXiv:2609.13463v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The increasing deployment of AI agents in long-horizon tasks yields massive execution logs. Diagnosing failures within these records is crucial for reliability, as it transforms outcome-level signals into actionable interventions. The sheer scale of the data renders human review impractical, driving the need for automated root-cause attribution (RCA). articles.summary: A paper frames root-cause attribution for long-horizon AI agent failures as a search problem, proposing continual search to handle large, sparse execution traces where LLM-based RCA has low accuracy.

articles.title: Governing at Machine Speed: An Adaptive Intelligence Architecture for Real-Time AI Policy Enforcement

articles.summary: A paper proposes an adaptive intelligence architecture for real-time AI policy enforcement, identifying an 'attestation deficit' where organizations have governance policies but cannot produce auditable, tamper-evident enforcement evidence within regulatory timelines.

articles.summary: The arXiv paper OrchSLM studies small language model orchestration for agentic pipelines, arguing specialized SLMs may better serve repetitive subtasks than monolithic LLMs despite limited capacity and context windows.

articles.summary: The arXiv paper introduces OdoBot, a web-agent architecture that models application behavior to complete tasks at a fraction of the token cost of conventional web agents.

articles.title: Fraglingo: Molecular Design via Attachment-Aware Autoregressive Fragment Generation

articles.summary: The Asclepius paper presents an adaptive harness for long-horizon clinical agents, tested in the Clinical Environment Simulator where agents managing an emergency-department shift reach correct diagnoses but fail to deliver complete care.

articles.title: AutoTailor: Automatic, User-Aligned Capability Selection and Adaptation for Web Agents
articles.snippet: arXiv:2609.13548v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Web agents can utilize reusable tools to reduce the cost and latency of low-level browser interaction, but automatically discovered tool collections can be large, redundant, and poorly aligned with user demand. articles.title: Competence-Gated Pooling of Language Models and Priors for Event Forecasting
articles.snippet: arXiv:2609.12101v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In hybrid forecasting, a language model is often one of several available signals. A system may already have a market, crowd, or statistical forecast and must decide whether the model adds useful information or should be ignored. The relevant target is therefore not standalone model accuracy, but relative competence, defined as the model's marginal value beyond the available external forecast. articles.summary: The paper frames hybrid event forecasting around a language model's relative competence — its marginal value beyond an existing market, crowd, or statistical forecast — and derives under Brier loss when model disagreement improves that external forecast.
articles.summaryZhHK: 篇論文將混合式事件預測嘅重點放喺語言模型嘅相對能力——即係喺已有市場、群眾或者統計預測之外嘅邊際價值——並喺 Brier loss 之下推導出幾時模型之間嘅分歧可以改善外部預測。

articles.title: Language Is an Insufficient Substrate for Quantitative Reasoning, and Consequential Domains Need Large Quantitative Models
articles.snippet: arXiv:2609.12105v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The prevailing assumption in applied machine learning is that progress on consequential quantitative decisions such as pricing risk, allocating capital, triaging patients, or containing a network intrusion will follow from progress in large language models (LLMs). articles.summary: The authors argue language is a lossy encoding of the quantitative record, so progress on consequential decisions like pricing risk, allocating capital, or triaging patients requires Large Quantitative Models rather than LLMs alone.

articles.title: Can LLMs in Draft-Verify-Revise Pipelines Resolve Deictic Ambiguity?
articles.snippet: arXiv:2609.12162v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Draft-verify-revise is a common LLM orchestration pattern for scaling inference-time compute. One LLM drafts, a second critiques the draft and provides feedback, and a third uses that feedback to revise the draft into the final output. As context cascades between stages, LLMs at different stages can resolve a context-dependent expression such as "previous" differently. articles.summary: The study examines whether draft-verify-revise LLM pipelines resolve deictic ambiguity, since context cascading between stages can shift what an expression like 'previous' refers to.

articles.title: GLARE: Generative Learning via Adversarial Reward Estimation For Social Dynamics Forecasting
articles.snippet: arXiv:2609.12165v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Meeting continuation requires tracking the agenda, speaker roles, participant intentions, and disagreement across long multi-party discussions. We introduce the Meeting Dynamic Forecasting Benchmark (MDFB), constructed from 2,207 real-world meetings and 24,794 future-facing queries. articles.summary: GLARE combines adversarial reward estimation with generative learning for social dynamics forecasting, and introduces the Meeting Dynamic Forecasting Benchmark (MDFB) built from 2,207 real meetings and 24,794 future-facing queries.

articles.title: WinSyn: An Automated Pipeline for Realistic Enterprise Question-Answering Evaluation
articles.snippet: arXiv:2609.12171v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Enterprise settings provide a challenging environment for question-answering agents, which often rely on Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Deep Research (DR), and related techniques. Much of this challenge comes from the complexity of enterprise data: information is often spread across evolving and potentially conflict- ing emails, chat messages, documents, and other artifacts. articles.summary: WinSyn is an automated pipeline for generating realistic enterprise question-answering evaluations, addressing benchmarks that lack real-world complexity, natural queries, and long-form responses.

articles.title: Soft Symbol Grounding for Prototypical Concepts
articles.snippet: arXiv:2609.12247v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Neuro-symbolic models are usually trained with supervision only on final labels, leaving the intermediate concepts unobserved. Since many concept assignments are consistent with a given label, training can predict labels correctly while recovering the wrong concepts, a failure known as a reasoning shortcut. articles.summary: The paper proposes soft symbol grounding for prototypical concepts to reduce reasoning shortcuts, avoiding the hand-crafted task-specific differentiable losses that couple perception and reasoning in existing neuro-symbolic methods.

articles.title: GTA: Graph Theory Agent and Benchmark for Algorithmic Graph Reasoning with LLMs
articles.snippet: arXiv:2609.12265v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly asked to reason over structured data such as graphs, yet how reliably they can carry out multi-step graph algorithms in language remains unclear. Existing evaluations tend to use simple tasks on small graphs, to score code generation rather than reasoning over the graph itself, or to fix a single input format. articles.summary: GTA introduces Graph Theory Bench (GT Bench), covering 24 classical graph problems across 44 task-structure settings with over 100,000 examples in four representations, plus an agent for algorithmic graph reasoning with LLMs.

articles.title: Learning Symbolic Constraint Representations from Examples: A Neuro-Symbolic Approach
articles.snippet: arXiv:2609.12267v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Learning user-defined concepts as constraint networks has been extensively studied in the constraint acquisition (CA) literature. However, existing approaches typically rely on intensive interactions with a human oracle, making the learning process costly in terms of time and number of queries. articles.summary: A neuro-symbolic framework for constraint acquisition trains Oracle Transformer models that emulate user responses, cutting the number of human queries needed to learn user-defined concepts as constraint networks.

articles.title: T-GADE: Thermodynamical Generative-AI-Driven Evolution of LLM Artifacts
articles.snippet: arXiv:2609.12286v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Integrating evolutionary computation and large language models (LLMs) requires control of population diversity as well as generative capability. Among LLM outputs, those with explicit structure, such as a description paired with code, are structured artifacts; we use artifact for short. articles.summary: T-GADE evolves structured LLM artifacts, such as a description paired with code, by extending thermodynamical genetic algorithms with LLM-based genetic operators and artifact-level diversity evaluation under a free-energy objective.

articles.title: AIM: A Privacy-Aware Interoperable Memory Framework for Multi-Agent Multi-User LLM Systems
articles.snippet: arXiv:2609.12320v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Traditional large language models (LLMs) are scoped to individual user sessions, limiting their knowledge to a single conversation and preventing them from learning user preferences that evolve over time. articles.summary: AIM is a privacy-aware interoperable memory framework that lets multi-agent, multi-user LLM systems share public knowledge and learn evolving user preferences beyond individual sessions.

articles.title: Affective Agent: On-Device Personalized Intervention Reasoning for Wearable Systems
articles.snippet: arXiv:2609.12322v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Affective computing has advanced wearable state inference, but on-device reasoning about whether, when, and how to intervene remains challenging. We present Affective Agent, a three-layer reference architecture for personalized intervention reasoning under uncertainty on wearable-class hardware. articles.summary: Affective Agent is a three-layer on-device reference architecture pairing a sub-billion-parameter language model with physiological evidence, context, and user history to decide whether, when, and how to intervene via wearables, without cloud dependency or per-user retraining.

articles.title: Toward Robust Personalized Alignment for LLMs: Mitigating Persona Drift in Multi-Turn Dialogue
articles.snippet: arXiv:2609.12373v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Persona drift remains a central challenge for personalized language models, as user profiles evolve over long interactions rather than remain permanently fixed. articles.summary: Researchers introduce Probabilistic Focal Search (PFS), which mixes heuristic-guided and minimum-f expansions to accelerate bounded-suboptimal search by advancing the lower bound.

articles.summary: A paper proposes operational resilience and considerate participation as complementary ways to evaluate generative AI agents facing accumulating technical, human, and operational disruptions.

articles.title: Studying Without a Syllabus: Task-Agnostic Environment Preprocessing
articles.snippet: arXiv:2609.10824v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Before an LLM agent tackles tasks in a new environment, it can inspect available corpora and tools and construct reusable resources such as indices, scripts, or procedural guidance. articles.snippet: arXiv:2609.10873v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Independent evaluation can reject harmful policy updates yet also prevent useful continual learning. articles.snippet: arXiv:2609.10964v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agentic LLM workflows consist of sequences of model turns interleaved with tool interactions, so their end-to-end completion time depends not only on inference speed but also on when ready turns are released. articles.title: Demystifying the Privacy-Utility Trade-off in LLM Interactions
articles.snippet: arXiv:2609.10992v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The integration of Large Language Models into daily tasks relies on context-rich instructions, inevitably exposing sensitive user information. articles.title: Defining AI Agents: A Compendium of Criteria, Metrics, and Benchmarks
articles.snippet: arXiv:2609.11018v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The term agent in artificial intelligence lacks a standard definition, complicating the evaluation, comparison, and reproducibility of AI agent research. articles.title: MOSAIC: Query-Aware Exploration Policy Adaptation for GraphRAG

articles.title: Beyond Right and Wrong: Evaluating Second-order Social Reasoning in Large Language Models
articles.snippet: arXiv:2609.05437v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Previous AI alignment efforts have focused primarily on first-order social norms -- teaching models what is socially acceptable or unacceptable (e.g., `do not steal'). However, social intelligence depends not only on norm recognition, but also on anticipating who will enforce it and how (e.g., public shame or even imprisonment). articles.summary: This paper introduces a framework for evaluating metanorm reasoning in LLMs—second-order social expectations about how people respond when rules are broken. It aims to move beyond first-order norms like 'do not steal' to capture deeper social intelligence.
articles.summaryZhHK: 呢篇論文提出一個評估 LLM 中 metanorm 推理嘅框架——即係關於規則被打破時人哋點樣回應嘅二階社會期望。佢旨在超越好似「唔好偷嘢」呢啲一階規範，去捕捉更深層嘅社會智能。

articles.title: CriticGen: Generation-Aware Evaluation as Actionable Feedback
articles.snippet: arXiv:2609.05439v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Current evaluation methods for large language models are coarse-grained and decoupled from generation, producing generic explanations that fail to provide actionable feedback for model improvement. We propose CriticGen, a fine-grained, generation-aware evaluation framework that turns evaluation into actionable control for answer improvement. articles.summary: CriticGen is a fine-grained, generation-aware evaluation framework that turns evaluation into actionable control for answer improvement. It generates sample-specific evaluation dimensions and scoring criteria to provide actionable feedback for model improvement.

articles.title: When Does Memory Help? A Cost-Aware Evaluation of Long-Term Memory in Tool-Using LLM Agents
articles.snippet: arXiv:2609.05441v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Long-term memory for LLM agents is evaluated today by conversational recall benchmarks (LoCoMo, LongMemEval), which measure question answering over dialogue history, not whether remembered facts change what a tool-using agent does. We present MERIT (Memory Evaluation for Realistic Instrumented Tasks), a benchmark and harness that measures the marginal utility of memory for task-executing agents under explicit cost accounting. articles.summary: This paper presents MERIT, a benchmark and harness that measures the marginal utility of long-term memory for tool-using LLM agents under explicit cost accounting. It provides episodic tool-use tasks across three domains to evaluate whether remembered facts change agent behavior.
articles.summaryZhHK: 呢篇論文介紹 MERIT，一個 benchmark 同 harness，用嚟喺明確成本核算下衡量長期記憶對使用工具嘅 LLM agent 嘅邊際效用。佢提供三個領域嘅 episodic tool-use 任務，評估記住嘅事實會唔會改變 agent 行為。

articles.title: AutoFyn Technical Report: Non-Parametric Expert Iteration for Long-Horizon Agents
articles.snippet: arXiv:2609.05446v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce AutoFyn, an agent harness inspired by the Expert Iteration algorithm, adapting a frozen model across many rounds by updating persistent state from verified reward signals rather than model weights. Each round begins from a fresh model session, and durable information is reintroduced only through explicit interfaces such as persistent memory files, reports, and repository state. articles.summary: AutoFyn is an agent harness inspired by Expert Iteration that adapts a frozen model by updating persistent state from verified reward signals rather than model weights. It uses an orchestrator to explore and plan multiple approaches with specialized agents in each round.

articles.title: Damage-Aware Bandit Pruning for Vision and Language Transformers
articles.snippet: arXiv:2609.05448v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Structured post-training pruning of transformers requires selecting complete functional units whose suppression causes limited degradation. We formulate structured-unit selection for language and vision transformers as a damage-aware multi-armed bandit problem under a fixed candidate-evaluation budget. articles.summary: This paper formulates structured-unit pruning for language and vision transformers as a damage-aware multi-armed bandit problem under a fixed evaluation budget. articles.summaryZhHK: 呢篇論文將語言同視覺 transformer 嘅結構化單元剪枝，表述為固定評估預算下一個 damage-aware 多臂老虎機問題。佢喺校準批次上遮罩 attention heads 同 MLP channel groups，用 paired damage 指標嚟減少批次差異。

articles.title: Compiling VGDL into Causal Models
articles.snippet: arXiv:2609.05459v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reinforcement learning and large language models often struggle to accurately capture the causal mechanics of game environments. Standard reinforcement learning agents tend to rely on spurious correlations, while large language models are prone to hallucinating game rules. articles.summary: This paper proposes a deterministic framework that compiles games specified in the Video Game Description Language (VGDL) into causal models. It aims to improve RL and LLM agents' ability to capture the causal mechanics of game environments.
articles.summaryZhHK: 呢篇論文提出一個確定性框架，將用 Video Game Description Language (VGDL) 指定嘅遊戲編譯成因果模型。佢旨在改善 RL 同 LLM agent 捕捉遊戲環境因果機制嘅能力。

articles.title: SciLitBench: Benchmark and Design Principles for LLM-Powered Systematic Literature Reviews
articles.snippet: arXiv:2609.05505v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Systematic reviews require sustained human judgment across thousands of records, yet existing evaluations of large language models (LLMs) typically examine review stages in isolation. We introduce SciLitBench, a multi-stage benchmark spanning title and abstract screening, full-text screening, and schema-guided data extraction, with 42,981 retrieved records, 1,012 full texts, and annotations for 888 included papers. articles.summary: SciLitBench is a multi-stage benchmark for LLM-powered systematic literature reviews, covering screening and data extraction stages with over 42,000 retrieved records. Evaluation across 22 open-weight LLMs shows explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria improve title and abstract screening performance.
articles.summaryZhHK: SciLitBench 係一個用於 LLM 驅動系統性文獻回顧嘅多階段 benchmark，涵蓋篩選同數據提取階段，有超過 42,000 條檢索記錄。對 22 個 open-weight LLM 嘅評估顯示，明確嘅納入/排除標準可改善標題同摘要篩選表現。

articles.title: SCAFFOLD: Self-Improving Web Agents via Recursive Parametric Skill Abstraction
articles.snippet: arXiv:2609.05511v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Web agents need to navigate visually rich, long-horizon interfaces that change across sites, yet most previous agents still learn each task in isolation and discard the procedural knowledge they accumulate. articles.summary: SCAFFOLD is a self-improving framework for visual web agents that induces parametric, executable skills and compresses redundancy recursively. It enables agents to accumulate procedural knowledge across tasks rather than learning each one in isolation.
articles.summaryZhHK: SCAFFOLD 係一個用於視覺網頁 agent 嘅自我改進框架，可以歸納參數化、可執行嘅技能，並遞迴壓縮冗餘。佢令 agent 可以跨任務累積程序性知識，而唔係孤立噉學每個任務。

articles.title: Reasoning-Aware Compression: Identifying and Protecting Vulnerable Reasoning Circuits for Energy-Efficient LLM Deployment
articles.snippet: arXiv:2609.05512v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large Reasoning Models (LRMs) impose substantial energy costs during deployment, yet current compression methods apply uniform quantization across all components, risking damage to critical reasoning circuits. articles.summary: This paper presents a reasoning-aware compression framework that benchmarks quantization conditions across five reasoning benchmarks with hardware-level energy measurement. articles.title: When and What to Teach: Budget-Aware Online Adaptation for Web Agents
articles.snippet: arXiv:2609.05513v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Web agents have achieved significant success in automating complex internet tasks but deploying them in real-world environments requires continuous online adaptation. articles.title: The Failure Happens Before the Drift: The Social Dynamics of Values in LLM Agent Societies
articles.snippet: arXiv:2609.05514v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large Language Model (LLM)-based agents are increasingly used as proxies for human participants in social science research, yet it remains unclear whether they can faithfully simulate diverse and conflicting human value systems. articles.summary: This paper presents a World Values Survey-grounded simulation framework where culturally diverse LLM agents engage in value-laden discussions. Across roughly 4,000 conversations with 1,200 personas and three models, it examines social dynamics and value drift in agent societies.

articles.title: Beyond "AI Helps Humans": Decision-Targeted Evaluation Design for Human-Agent Teams in the Agentic Era
articles.snippet: arXiv:2609.05527v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Wherever a coding agent works under engineer supervision, or a clinical model assists a radiologist, the deployment question is whether to keep the human-AI workflow or replace it with the human alone or the agent alone. The human-AI workflow is worth keeping only if it beats both of those alternatives. articles.summary: This paper proposes decision-targeted evaluation design for human-AI teams, addressing whether to keep a human-AI workflow or replace it with human alone or agent alone. It handles fixed replay budgets by deciding which tasks to replay to observe alternative outcomes.

articles.title: EdgeMem: LLM-Free Agent Memory Construction and Retrieval via Evidence-Preserving Multi-Anchor Hypergraph

articles.summary: EdgeMem is an agent-memory method that preserves original interaction turns and organizes them through complementary content, temporal, and episodic cues via a multi-anchor hypergraph. It avoids LLM-generated summaries to reduce cost and retain answer-bearing details.

articles.title: EnvCraft: Synthesizing Executable Environments in Agentic RL for Claw-like Agent
articles.snippet: arXiv:2609.05576v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The paradigm of LLMs has rapidly shifted from passive language interfaces to autonomous Claw-like agents that execute long-horizon tasks across stateful workspaces. articles.summary: EnvCraft synthesizes executable environments for agentic RL in claw-like agents, addressing the scarcity of interactive training environments. It goes beyond tool-calling endpoints to support end-to-end real-world task demands.

articles.title: Agents Trust Tools Too Much: Measuring Reliance on Unreliable Tools
articles.snippet: arXiv:2609.05587v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Existing evaluations of tool-using agents primarily measure whether an agent can successfully complete diverse tasks with tools. articles.summary: This paper investigates how agents respond to unreliable tool returns by evaluating fourteen LLMs with three tools—web search, LLM sub-agent delegation, and code execution. It corrupts tool returns to measure whether agents adopt corrupted content in their final outputs.
